title: Bump the crate to 0.13.3 for the skill edit
body:
**Chose:** bump the version to 0.13.3 in Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, skills/bundle.lock and the cockpit mod's three version pins (plugin.json, register.tsx, cockpit.test.tsx).
**Over:** leaving the version at 0.13.2, which `bundle_lock_matches` refuses ("skills changed since 0.13.2: bump Cargo.toml past 0.13.2 first"), and `cockpit_mod` pins plugin.json to the crate version.
**Because:** a skill edit cannot ship under the old version, and the slice did not name the bump; files outside the slice's list had to move with it.
**Undo:** set the six pins back and rewrite the lock once another skill edit carries the bump.

title: Where review second prints skipped files, and what a failed check-attr says
body:
**Chose:** `review second` prints the `skipped:` block after the reviewer probe succeeds, right before the first pass, so a probe failure still starts its output with `unreviewed:`. With nothing kept it prints one line, `unreviewed: no changes against <base> left after skipping <paths>`. A failed `git check-attr` writes `skipped: vendored and generated files not checked (<error>)` and still skips the tool-written files under it.
**Over:** printing the block before the probe, which would push the `unreviewed:` reason off the first line; failing the run on a check-attr error.
**Because:** the slice fixed the block's content and the defensive default, but not its place relative to the probe or the exact wording.
**Undo:** move the `skipped` write in `second()` (src/cli/review.rs) above the probe; reword `Skip::lines` in src/review.rs.

title: The no-push hook refuses any shell command containing a Rust .push( call
body: A python heredoc that edited Rust containing `out.push(` was refused as a `git push`. Use the Edit tool for source edits that contain `push`.

title: A second skill edit under an already-bumped, uncommitted version makes FACTORY_BUNDLE_WRITE refuse
body: Restore the lock first with `git checkout -- skills/bundle.lock`, then run `FACTORY_BUNDLE_WRITE=1 cargo test -q --test skills_bundle` once. The bump itself also moves the cockpit mod's three version pins, which `tests/cockpit_mod.rs` checks.

title: What a part's reviewer prompt says
body:
**Chose:** a part's prompt opens "Part k of n of the diff of <path> against <base> is in <file>", and the progress line on stderr reads `review pass i/N: <path> (part k of n) (L lines)`. `diff_prompt` now takes that opening phrase instead of the file list.
**Over:** the unchanged "The diff of <path>" wording, which would let a reviewer report the missing hunks as a defect.
**Because:** the slice fixed the heading and the diff file but said nothing about the prompt text.
**Undo:** in src/review.rs `diff_pass_prompt`, build `what` as `The diff of …` for parts too.

title: How an oversized hunk is cut, and a diff that cannot be read
body:
**Chose:** a hunk over the cap is cut into ceil(changed / cap) even chunks (1,500 lines → 3 × 500, 601 → 301 + 300); context after a chunk's last change stays with it; git's function-context text after `@@` stays on the first chunk only. When `git diff` of a file to split fails, the file stays one pass, whose prompt then reports the same error as unreviewed.
**Over:** cap-sized chunks with a small remainder (600, 600, 300; 600, 1); failing the whole review on that read.
**Because:** "about pass_lines" leaves the size open, and even chunks avoid a one-line pass; a failing pass already has its own unreviewed line.
**Undo:** set `size = cap` in `cut_hunk`; return the error from `review::plan`.

title: The owner's git config writes mnemonic diff prefixes (c/ i/)
body: A unit test that runs `git diff` itself outside the harness fixture gets `diff --git c/f i/f`; pass `--src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/` (tests/review.rs fixtures already isolate the config).

title: after slice-05
body:
**Covers:** slices 01, 02, 05
**Gate:** 1 run, 0 red, about 2 min — caught: nothing (cargo check, the full cargo test suite, the cockpit plugin validation and its 14 bun tests all green, per gates/1-1.log). Leaks: 3.4% comment share, clean.
**Prove:** FR-1, FR-2, FR-3, FR-4, FR-5 (skill row), FR-7 and FR-8 driven and green, 11 tests in all — evidence: cp-1/fr-1-security-range.txt, cp-1/fr-2-timeouts.txt, cp-1/fr-3-skipped-files.txt, cp-1/fr-4-huge-file-split.txt, cp-1/fr-5-skill-sources.txt, cp-1/fr-7-ux-first.txt, cp-1/fr-8-autonomy-rows.txt. Not reached: FR-5's three review tests (`feature_puts_settled_decisions_in_every_pass_prompt`, `a_superseded_decision_is_left_out`, `no_feature_keeps_the_prompt_as_today`) do not exist yet. They are slice-03's, which this checkpoint does not cover, and `cargo test --test review` finds 0 of them.
**Fixed:** none

title: How the settled block and the since range read in a pass prompt
body:
**Chose:** the block is appended after the diff instruction as "Settled for this feature: a finding that contradicts an entry below must name the entry and say why it is wrong.", then `Decisions taken:` with one `- AD-n — title: chose` line each, then the PRD's Decisions log and Non-goals sections verbatim with their headings; `--others` comes after it. A since pass's prompt says "The diff of … since commit <sha> is in …". Over the cap, after the Non-goals and every decision are gone, the end of the Decisions log is cut too. `review second --doc` accepts `--feature` and ignores it. Only an entry after an AD can supersede it.
**Over:** a separate instruction per part; "against <sha>" wording, which reads like a base branch; failing or returning an over-cap block when the Decisions log alone exceeds 32 KiB.
**Because:** the slice fixed the parts, the cut order and the 32 KiB cap but not the wording, the order beside `--others`, or a Decisions log that alone breaks the cap.
**Undo:** reword `with_settled` and `Range::against` in src/review.rs; drop the last branch of `fit` in src/settled.rs.
